texts.firmware.soundfont_sf2.about: A SoundFont 2 file (.sf2) that the games' MIDI music is played with, used when 'Use custom MIDI soundfont' is on. Any soundfont can be used; the project records exactly which file it was. None comes with the package.
texts.setting.compatfantasyzonefix.about: Fantasy Zone's 176x208 version mirrors its images in a way the phones' standard does not allow, and is wrong even on real phones. This draws it as the game means, and breaks other games that use the same drawing for Nokia Series 40 phones. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatignorevolumechanges.about: Ignores the game's changes of volume. Some games change the volume of sounds they already stopped, which can break the playback. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatimmediaterepaints.about: A J2ME game's requests to redraw its screen are normally queued. This handles them at once, which can help a game that freezes waiting for its own drawing. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatmascotv3fovfix: MascotCapsule V3 horizontal field of view fix
texts.setting.compatmascotv3fovfix.about: For games drawn with the MascotCapsule V3 3D engine: it can help a game made for an upright screen when it runs on a screen on its side, or on another size than its own. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatnotranslatedrawrgb.about: Draws pixel arrays (drawRGB) without the drawing origin's offset. Sony Ericsson's versions of some games, Peggle for one, expect that, as their phones did. Turn it on when things are missing in a Sony Ericsson game. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatoverrideplatformchecks.abo: Some games check which phone they run on by its name (Nokia, Siemens S60) and refuse others. This answers with FreeJ2ME's own name, so those games start. FreeJ2ME-Plus turns it on by default, as it helps far more often than it breaks. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatrepaintonsetcurrent.about: Redraws a screen when the game brings it forward. J2ME does not do that by itself; a game is supposed to. This fixes games that stay on a blank or black screen when they start, which is often the case for games with 3D (M3G) graphics. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compatsiemensdrawing.about: Draws images the way some Siemens games, such as Swedish Touring Car Championship, need when the drawing origin is negative. It breaks other games. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.compattranslatetoorigin: Translate to origin on Graphics reset
texts.setting.compattranslatetoorigin.about: Moves the drawing origin back to the corner of the screen before every draw. Some games expect that instead of keeping track of it themselves. It also helps when what a game draws keeps sliding in one direction. One of FreeJ2ME-Plus's compatibility settings, which help some games at the expense of others. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.customsoundfont.about: Plays the games' MIDI music with a soundfont (.sf2) you give, in place of the sounds Java comes with, so the music can sound like it did on a particular phone. When it is on, the project asks for the soundfont as firmware and records which file it was. The soundfont is in the machine's memory, so a large one makes every savestate larger by about its size. Soundfonts may be copyrighted: share a project, not the soundfont. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.dojaversion.about: The version of NTT Docomo's i-appli platform (DoJa, later Star) the phone has, for DoJa games. A game can behave differently on another version, and some need the one they were made for. Star-2.0, the newest, is the default. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.fpslimit.about: The most pictures a second FreeJ2ME lets the game draw; 'off' lets a game draw as often as it asks. Games differ, and the right value is the one the game was made for. FreeJ2ME-Plus's maintainer reports that most DoJa games want 60, and that a few, such as Castlevania for DoJa, run slowly unless it is off, because DoJa games keep their own time and a limit from outside fights it. Bubble Smile, from Samsung phones, drew 3 or 4 pictures a second on them and runs too fast above that. Bounce Tales draws as fast as it can and its physics follow the rate. Above 60, more than one picture can be drawn in a frame; Chimera shows the last. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.m3gperspectivecorrection.about: Whether textures on 3D (M3G) surfaces are drawn with the depth taken into account. 'App-Controlled' does what the game asks. Forcing it on or off can correct a camera's view or where drawing stops in some games. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.m3gperspectivequality.about: How finely the perspective correction above divides a 3D surface. Higher is closer to the right picture and costs more time a frame. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.midisynths.about: How many MIDI tunes can play at once, each on a synthesizer of its own (FreeJ2ME's own setting). More cost more time a frame. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.phone.about: Which maker's key codes the keys send. Phones of different makers numbered the arrows and the soft keys differently, and a game made for one reads those numbers. 'Standard' is Nokia's, which most games use; choose the maker a game was made for if its keys do nothing. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.screensize.about: The phone's screen, in pixels, width by height. A J2ME game draws for the screen it is given; many were made for one size and draw only part of a larger screen. 240x320 is the most common. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sound.about: 'off' gives the game no sound at all: its players start and play silence. A game may behave differently without sound (one that waits for a tune to end), so this is part of the machine, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.textencoding.about: How the game's text is read. 'auto' is what FreeJ2ME chooses: Korean (EUC_KR) for an SKT game (.msd beside it), Japanese (Shift_JIS) for a KDDI game (.kjx) or with a DoJa descriptor (.jam) beside it, else ISO_8859_1. A Chinese game is never chosen for, as nothing in its files says it is one: choose GBK for Simplified Chinese (mainland China; it reads GB2312 too) and Big5 for Traditional Chinese (Taiwan, Hong Kong). A game that asks for another one than it was started with is not started, and says which to choose here. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.game.help: The game: its .jar, and the descriptor that came with it if there is one (.jad, or .jam for DoJa, .msd for SKT games), which FreeJ2ME reads for the game's properties. A KDDI game is one .kjx file. The files are never changed.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the game had saved (its record stores) at the start, for a project that begins from a saved game: the .zip Emulator > Export Save Data... writes. The file is never changed. Save data of another game is refused. Leave this empty to start with nothing saved.
texts.slot.savedata.name_help: save data is identified by its extension, .zip.
